title: Black clay jar
summary: In the Oaxaca valley, potters raise jars and pitchers from grey clay, rub the leather-hard surface with a smooth quartz stone until it shines, and fire it in a smothered kiln that turns the clay black. Some pieces are cut with fine pierced patterns before firing. Here you shape a jar and choose the finish of each band.
howToPlay: Look at the lit jar on its shelf: it shows the shape and the finish of each band.
Drag across the turning clay to set how wide each row is.
Press Glaze, then tap a band and a finish: burnished black, matt grey-black or raw clay.
Press Check to see your stars, or Watch and learn to see a round played for you.
rules: Shape counts for 70 percent of the score: the closer each of the 12 rows is to the width of the lit target, the better.
Finish counts for 30 percent: a band scores when it carries the same swatch as the target.
A pierced band, a polished band and a matt band are different finishes in the picture; the three finishes are the three swatches.
Undo takes back one stroke; Reshape goes back to the clay; Reset starts the shape again.
Three stars for 88 or more, two stars for 65 and one star for 40.
heritageNote: Black clay pottery is made in the Oaxaca valley of southern Mexico, most of all in San Bartolo Coyotepec. A piece is shaped by hand, polished with a stone while the clay is leather-hard, and fired in a smothered kiln that darkens the clay and keeps the shine.
